docs.title: HomeTiles
docs.text:
HomeTiles is free, open-source firmware that turns a supported touch display into a Home Assistant control panel. Use tiles to switch lights, adjust heating, control music, and see sensor or energy data at a glance.

docs.title: Advanced Setup
docs.text: Details for the Installation: manual flashing, what the display asks, setups without HACS or with an MQTT broker, and older displays.

docs.title: Manual Flashing
docs.text:
If the browser installer is unavailable, use Espressif's Flash Download Tool or esptool. This alternative is for a first installation or full reset and erases all settings. Export your dashboard first if needed.

  1. Download the exact device's _factory.bin from the latest release. Match the complete model and revision; V1/V2, LCD-7/LCD-7B and P4/S3 images are not interchangeable.

  2. In Flash Download Tool, select ESP32-P4 or ESP32-S3, UART, and the USB port. Erase the flash, then write the factory file at 0x0. Alternatively, with esptool installed:

    python -m esptool --port COM3 chip-id
python -m esptool --port COM3 write-flash --erase-all 0x0 your_device_factory.bin

    Replace COM3 with your serial port (for example /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux), and the filename with your downloaded factory image.

  3. Wait until verification finishes, then restart the display.

ESP32-P4 revision check: standard P4 images require pre-v3 silicon (revisions 1 to 199). The experimental Waveshare 7B and 10.1 _rev3 images and the Guition JC8012P4A1 V3 image are for v3.1 and newer, including v3.2. Check the chip-id output before a manual write. esptool does not enforce HomeTiles' narrower revision checks.

Never write a plain update .bin at 0x0. To preserve settings, use the browser's Update mode or Firmware Updates.

docs.title: Flashing Problems
docs.text:
• No serial port: use a data cable, try another USB port, and close other serial monitors or flashing tools.
  • Cannot connect: hold BOOT while connecting, then release it when the connection starts.
  • Wrong chip or revision: recheck the device label and selected model; do not bypass the check.
  • Interrupted installation: reconnect and repeat the selected operation. An interrupted Update keeps the previous app; an interrupted factory reset needs a complete factory installation.

For a blank display after flashing or connection problems after setup, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: The First-Start Setup
docs.text:
A new display opens a setup in four steps. You can leave it at any time and finish it later under Settings → System → Setup.

  1. Basic settings: language, time zone, light or dark theme, and the rotation. New ESP32-P4 displays that can stand upright also ask for landscape or upright.
  2. Connect to WiFi: choose your network. Without a network, switch on Hotspot and set up the WiFi from your phone (password 12345678).
  3. Add to Home Assistant: tap Pair; the display can be found for two minutes. Home Assistant shows Panel found, then the same six-digit number as the display. Confirm it in Home Assistant with Numbers match: connect and on the display with Confirm.
  4. Add your tiles: the address of the Web Admin; open it in your computer's browser.

docs.title: Pairing
docs.text:
Pairing needs no password: the display accepts it only within the two minutes after you tapped Pair, so only someone standing at the display can pair it. Afterwards Settings → System shows Home Assistant: Connected with Direct · Bridge and its address, and Pairing: Paired.

The display connects to Home Assistant on TCP ports 8140–8147, camera tiles additionally on 8124–8131. If your network separates them, allow these ports from the display to the Home Assistant host. Home Assistant finds the display by mDNS, so both need to be in the same network.

To unpair, open Pairing under Settings → System → Security on the display and tap Unpair, or use Security in the Bridge options; the other side follows. An unpaired display counts as a new display and can be paired again.

docs.title: Choosing Entities
docs.text:
With a Web Admin password, the entity picker of a paired display finds every entity in Home Assistant. Set it like this:

  1. On the display, open Settings → System → Security and tap Allow next to Web Admin password.
  2. Within two minutes, set the password in the Web Admin under Settings → System.

Without a password, the picker offers only the entities selected under HomeTiles Bridge → Configure → Entity configuration. For Energy tiles, also enable the electricity, gas or water category under Configure → Energy Dashboard.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Protection What it does Pairing Every message between display and Bridge is encrypted and signed, commands as well as states. A recorded command cannot be sent again. Web Admin password Only you can change the dashboard and the display's settings. Locks and alarm panels Work only on a paired display with a Web Admin password. Home Assistant checks their codes; see Lock. PINs Settings and folders can ask for a PIN on the display. This is a child lock, not a login.

docs.title: Multiple Displays
docs.text: Pair each display the same way. Every display becomes its own device of the HomeTiles Bridge and gets its own topic name automatically. Entity selections in the Bridge options are shared by all displays.

docs.title: Without The Button
docs.text:
Add it to HACS by hand: in HACS, open Custom repositories from the menu, add https://github.com/GalusPeres/HomeTiles-Bridge as an Integration, download HomeTiles Bridge, and restart Home Assistant.

Without HACS: copy custom_components/tab5_lvgl from the Bridge repository into Home Assistant's custom_components directory and restart.

docs.title: Moving From MQTT To The Direct Link
docs.text:
A display set up over MQTT with an older version keeps working after the update. To move it to the direct link:

  1. Update the Bridge to v0.9.0 and the display to HomeTiles v0.9.0.
  2. On the display, tap Pair under Settings → System → Security.
  3. Home Assistant shows Connect the panel for the existing device. Select Submit and compare the number.
Connect the panel

The device keeps its entry, area, names and entities. The MQTT settings stay saved on the display but are no longer used. Encryption that was set up over MQTT is replaced by the pairing of the direct link.

docs.title: Using An MQTT Broker
docs.text:
The direct link needs no broker. If you prefer MQTT, for example to use the display's topics elsewhere:

  1. Install an MQTT broker. On Home Assistant OS, install the Mosquitto broker app under Settings → Apps, start it, and add a Home Assistant user for it under Settings → People → Users. Confirm the discovered MQTT integration. Other installations: see the official MQTT setup.
  2. Open the display's Web Admin, go to Settings → System → MQTT, and enter the broker's IP address, port 1883, username and password. With the Mosquitto app, use the Home Assistant machine's IP, not core-mosquitto. Keep the suggested Device topic base and Home Assistant prefix.
  3. Select Save. Home Assistant shows Panel discovered under Settings → Devices & services; select Add.

Without discovery, add the panel under Add Integration → HomeTiles Bridge with the same topic base and prefix. Pairing always uses the direct link: tapping Pair moves an MQTT display to it.

docs.title: Bridge Integration
docs.text:
The HomeTiles Bridge connects your displays to Home Assistant: directly over an encrypted link, or over an MQTT broker. It shares entity data and sends tile actions back to Home Assistant, with each display listed as its own device.

Displays in the HomeTiles Bridge integration

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You need Home Assistant 2025.11 or newer and HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.4 for all documented features with firmware v0.9.4. The direct link needs no MQTT broker. Follow the Installation to install the Bridge and pair your first display.

HACS provides Bridge updates. After an update, restart Home Assistant. For additional displays, follow Multiple displays.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Open Settings → Devices & Services → HomeTiles Bridge → Configure.

docs.title: Panel Settings
docs.text: Field Setting Base topic The display's topic name. Pairing sets it; over MQTT it must match Device topic base in the display's MQTT settings. Each display needs a unique value. HA prefix Default: ha/statestream. Use the same value on the Bridge and all displays. Device name / manufacturer / model Optional details shown in Home Assistant.

docs.title: Entity Configuration
docs.text:
A paired display with a Web Admin password does not need these lists: its entity picker finds every entity in Home Assistant, and the display tells the Bridge which entities its tiles use. Displays without a password, and displays on MQTT, offer the entities selected here.

Select the sensors, binary sensors, numbers, selects, date/time entities, weather, lights, switchable entities, covers, fans, locks, alarm panels, climate entities, media players, cameras, images, and scenes/scripts/buttons you want to use. Then assign them to tiles in the Web Admin.

Selections are shared across all displays. Action aliases are generated automatically and remain stable when selections are reordered; custom aliases use one alias=entity_id per line.

Switches / switchable entities accepts switch, input_boolean, automation, fan, humidifier, remote, and siren. They use the existing Switch tile and its on/off popup; lights retain brightness/color controls. Automations are enabled/disabled. Fan and Siren require HA support for both on and off.

Scenes / Scripts / Buttons accepts scene, script, button, and input_button. Assign these to the Button tile (called Scene before v0.9.2): a tap activates the scene, starts the script without parameters, or presses the button once. See the compatibility table for exact behavior and limits. Use updated firmware for the complete availability handling and translated editor labels.

Older display configurations, entity selections, aliases, and MQTT topic names remain valid. Commands must target selected entities; retained switch/action commands are ignored on reconnect.

Numbers accepts number and input_number; Selects accepts select and input_select; Date/Time accepts time, date, datetime, and input_datetime. Use their dedicated editable tile types. State, writable limits, options, availability, and history come from Home Assistant. Recorder exclusions also apply to these history views.

Fans, Locks, and Alarm panels feed the Fan, Lock, and Alarm Panel tiles (Bridge v0.8.0). Locks and alarm panels can only be operated from a paired display with a Web Admin password. Codes for locks and alarm panels lets the Bridge check the codes of devices that ignore a wrong code; Allow opening without a code is only for devices without their own code. Fans also remain selectable as switchable entities.

Calendars feed the Calendar tile. The Bridge reads their events from Home Assistant and publishes them retained on ha_prefix/calendar/<object>/events: when an event starts or ends, and every 15 minutes.

Bridge v0.9.0 remains compatible with older firmware and existing configurations. New features require the corresponding firmware; no reset or re-pairing is needed for a normal update.

docs.title: Display Settings
docs.text:
The display's Home Assistant device has its settings under Configuration: Display Brightness, Screensaver Brightness, Display Standby and Display Standby After, and with HomeTiles and Bridge v0.9.4:

Entity Use Theme Dark, Light or Automatic (light by day, dark at night), the same choice as under Settings → Display on the display. Display Rotation The steps the display offers: 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° on displays that turn in quarter turns, 0° and 180° on the others.

With older firmware the display keeps the former Display Rotation switch for 180° and has no Theme select.

docs.title: Control the Displayed View
docs.text:
Each compatible display exposes a View Select entity (Ansicht in German) on its existing Home Assistant device, next to the display controls. It offers Home, configured folders including nested folders, and configured tiles with supported popups.

Choosing an option opens that target using the existing display navigation and popup. Manual navigation and closing a popup report the actual view back to HA. Opening another popup closes the previous one and releases its resources, including a camera stream. Folder PIN protection remains in effect.

Options contain the folder path and a stable target suffix, so identical names remain distinguishable. Renaming or moving a tile updates its label; deleting it removes the option. Titles with line breaks remain two lines on the display but become one line in this list. Update an automation's option text if you rename or move its target.

For example, use these actions after your doorbell trigger. Replace the Select entity and camera option with the exact values shown by your own display:

actions:
  - action: select.select_option
    target:
      entity_id: select.hall_display_view
    data:
      option: "Home / Entrance camera [t:12]"
  - delay: "00:00:20"
  - action: select.select_option
    target:
      entity_id: select.hall_display_view
    data:
      option: "Home"

Commands to offline displays or missing targets are rejected. Status updates do not navigate, and old commands are not replayed after a restart or MQTT reconnection. Camera targets are available only on ESP32-P4.

docs.title: Energy Dashboard
docs.text: Enable the electricity, gas, or water categories you need. Each requires the corresponding data in Home Assistant's Energy Dashboard. These selections are also shared across displays.

docs.title: Pairing and Encryption
docs.text:
Pairing connects a display to the Bridge over the direct link. Every message between them is encrypted and signed, commands as well as states, and each command runs at most once. Camera stream tokens travel encrypted too.

  1. On the display, tap Pair under Settings → System → Security (or in the first-start setup).
  2. Home Assistant shows Panel found under Settings → Devices & services → Discovered; a display that is already set up over MQTT shows Connect the panel. Select Add or Submit. Where Home Assistant cannot find displays over mDNS (Docker without host networking, VLANs), open Add integration → HomeTiles Bridge → Panel by IP address (direct connection) within the two minutes and enter the display's IP address (shown under Settings → WiFi); a fixed IP address for the display in the router helps (Bridge v0.9.4).
  3. The display and Home Assistant show the same six-digit number. Confirm only if both numbers match, in Home Assistant and on the display.

The Installation shows each step. To switch encryption off, unpair on the display or use Security in the Bridge options; the other side follows, and the display then counts as a new display.

Displays paired over MQTT with firmware v0.8.0 keep their encrypted commands until they are paired again; pairing moves them to the direct link. Protocol details: bridge-link.md and command-encryption.md.

docs.title: Local Hardware Entities
docs.text:
Configure GPIO switches, onboard relays, and DS18B20 inputs on the display's I/O tab. The Bridge adds them to that display's Home Assistant device automatically; they do not belong in the shared entity selection.

Saving an assignment announces it again. Deleting it makes the old Home Assistant entity unavailable. Names you changed manually in Home Assistant are preserved.

docs.title: Retired Automatic Sensors
docs.text:
Bridge migration removes obsolete integration-owned battery and external-temperature entries only when they do not match the display's reported capabilities. It also cleans the corresponding shared selections and configuration, so ordinary restart or re-pairing does not recreate them. Devices without implemented battery measurement no longer advertise a battery sensor.

Configured local I/O and supported sensors are preserved, as are explicitly selected user entities. This cleanup does not delete arbitrary entities because their name contains Tab5.

docs.title: Experimental Camera Transport
docs.text:
Camera tiles are available on ESP32-P4. Allow the display to reach the Home Assistant host on TCP ports 8124–8131. The Bridge sends display-sized JPEG frames directly over the local network; MQTT handles camera control.

Each open display uses its own stream. Video conversion uses Home Assistant CPU time, while snapshot cameras are limited by their source refresh rate. See Camera troubleshooting if no video appears.

docs.title: Built-in Camera
docs.text:
Displays with a camera can share it with Home Assistant. This needs HomeTiles v0.7.0 and Bridge v0.7.0 or newer.

Display Camera Guition JC8012P4A1 V2 and V1 Built-in OV02C10 Guition JC1060P470C V2, JC4880P443 Optional OV02C10 module on the CSI connector Waveshare ESP32-P4 7-inch, 8-inch, 10.1-inch Built-in OV5647 front camera Waveshare ESP32-P4 7B, 4.3-inch, 5-inch, 4B Optional OV5647 module on the CSI connector M5Stack Tab5 Built-in SC2356

Tested on the Guition JC8012P4A1 V2, Waveshare 8-inch, and M5Stack Tab5. On the other displays, use Rotation, Mirror image, or Swap red and blue under Advanced if the image appears turned or its colors are swapped.

  1. In the Web Admin, open Settings → Built-in camera and enable Allow Home Assistant to use the built-in camera, then press Save.
  2. The Bridge adds a Camera entity to the display's Home Assistant device, plus a Camera switch that pauses it.
  3. Open the camera in Home Assistant, or show it on another display with a Camera tile.

The display captures images only while Home Assistant asks for them. Opening the camera starts a live stream that uses the same TCP ports 8124–8131 as camera tiles; it stops a few seconds after the last viewer closes. While the camera is in use, the display shows the camera indicator. Tapping its pill ends the current stream.

Disabling the setting removes the entity. The paused switch keeps the entity but sends no images. A display cannot show its own camera in its own camera popup.

docs.title: Voice Assistant (early version)
docs.text:
ESP32-P4 displays with a speaker and microphone can play audio from Home Assistant and work as an Assist voice satellite. This needs HomeTiles v0.9.2 and Bridge v0.9.2. It is an early version: the display has no microphone button and no audio settings yet; everything is set in Home Assistant.

It runs on the Waveshare ESP32-P4 4B, 4.3-inch, 7-inch, 7B, 8-inch and 10.1-inch, the Guition JC8012P4A1 V1, V2 and V3, JC1060P470C V2 and JC4880P443, and the M5Stack Tab5. Displays with only a speaker connector need a speaker fitted. Tested on the Guition JC8012P4A1 V2, Waveshare 4B and 8-inch, and M5Stack Tab5. The ESP32-S3 displays have no voice support.

The Bridge adds these entities to the display's Home Assistant device while the display announces its speaker or microphone:

Entity Use Speaker Media player: plays sounds, music, announcements and spoken answers from Home Assistant, with title, position, pause and seeking, and sets the volume. The Bridge decodes every format and sends the display plain audio at the pace it plays (HomeTiles and Bridge v0.9.4 or newer). When a camera's stream has sound, the display plays it in step with the picture while the camera popup or full screen is open. While it plays, the display does not listen for its wake word. Assist Assist satellite: Home Assistant's voice pipeline listens through the display's microphone, and the answer plays on its speaker. Start Assist button Starts a voice request without a wake word. Listening The display listens for its wake word by itself. Off on a new display. Wake word Okay Nabu, Hey Jarvis or Alexa. Kept while Listening is off. Assistant The Assist pipeline the display uses. Finished speaking detection How quickly a request ends after you stop speaking. Microphone Off on a new display. Turning it on from Home Assistant needs a paired display.

It works on the direct link and over MQTT.

docs.title: MQTT Topics Reference
docs.text:
Entity states use <HA prefix>/<entity>/.... The Bridge publishes them itself; Home Assistant's MQTT Statestream integration is not required. On the direct link the same topics travel over the link instead of a broker.

Topic reference for debugging

{id} is the panel device ID; <base> is its unique base topic.

Topic Direction Purpose <base>/stat/connected Display → HA Connection status <base>/view/catalog/* Display → HA Available navigation targets <base>/stat/view Display → HA Confirmed current view <base>/cmnd/view HA → Display Navigate to a current target <base>/cmnd/value Display → HA Validated Number, Select, or Date/Time edit <base>/stat/value HA → Display Editable command result tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/bridge Display → HA Device and local I/O announcement tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/bridge/apply HA → Display Configuration tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/bridge/icons HA → Display Icon updates tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/history/* Both Sensor history tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/weather/* Both Weather forecasts tab5_lvgl/config/{id}/energy/* Both Energy data <base>/cmnd/light Display → HA Light controls <base>/cmnd/switch Display → HA Compatible on/off controls <base>/cmnd/media Display → HA Media controls <base>/cmnd/climate Display → HA Climate controls <base>/cmnd/cover Display → HA Cover controls <base>/cmnd/scene Display → HA Scene/script activation or button press <base>/cmnd/camera Display → HA Open/close a camera session <base>/stat/camera HA → Display Camera connection and status <base>/cmnd/local_camera HA → Display Still image or live stream request for the built-in camera <base>/stat/local_camera Display → HA Built-in camera status (ready, disabled, error) <base>/cmnd/display_brightness HA → Display Display brightness (1–100%) <base>/stat/display_brightness Display → HA Current display brightness <base>/cmnd/screensaver_brightness HA → Display Screensaver brightness (1–100%) <base>/stat/screensaver_brightness Display → HA Current screensaver brightness <base>/cmnd/display_theme HA → Display Theme (dark, light, auto) <base>/stat/display_theme Display → HA Current theme setting <base>/cmnd/display_rotation HA → Display Rotation in degrees (one of the display's steps) <base>/stat/display_rotation Display → HA Rotation and steps, {"degrees":90,"options":[0,90,180,270]} <base>/cmnd/io/{channel_id} HA → Display Local Switch command (ON / OFF) <base>/stat/io/{channel_id} Display → HA Local Switch or temperature state

docs.title: Device logs
docs.text:
Read live USB logs from any HomeTiles ESP32-P4 or ESP32-S3 device in desktop Chrome or Edge.

Your logs stay locally in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

Connect the display's USB data/debug port with a data cable. Close other serial tools, select Connect, then choose the port. Reproduce the issue, select Disconnect, then Copy log.

Connect Disconnect Loading log viewer… Device log Copy log Clear log Follow log

Older output or long lines were trimmed. Copy the log soon after reproducing the problem.

Browser storage is unavailable. Copy your log before reloading, closing this tab, or leaving the documentation.

Firmware flashing is using the serial connection. Wait for it to finish before connecting.

Enable JavaScript to connect to your display and read its serial log.

Capture continues while you browse this documentation. After reloading or flashing, select Connect to resume. Logs stay in this tab until you close it. Copy them first. Clear log removes the saved copy.

docs.title: Capture a restart
docs.text: Select Connect, then choose Settings → System → Restart on the display. Alternatively, briefly press the RESET button if your device has one. If USB disconnects, select Connect again when the port returns.

docs.title: No output or no port
docs.text:
Check the data cable and data/debug port; close other serial tools. Use the display's power supply and install any required USB driver.

For saved crash logs, see Screenshot & Diagnostics.

docs.title: On-Device UI
docs.text:
Tap tiles to control devices, open folders, or view details. Arrange the tiles in the Web Admin.

Home in the head bar layout

Every icon sits on a round circle, and a tile can be filled with its icon's color. Half-height tiles show their title and value next to the icon. Rules can color a tile by the state of an entity. Every tile type and its popup is shown under Tile Types.

docs.title: Head Bar And Pages
docs.text:
The head shows Home's icon and title on the left, the page dots in the middle, and the time and the gear for Settings on the right. In a folder the head shows the folder's name, and the X goes back.

Up to five folders can be pages beside Home; choose them in the Web Admin. The dots show which page is open:

  • Swipe sideways anywhere on a page to turn it. Sliders and bars keep their own touch. On Home, a swipe from left to right opens the screensaver; over the screensaver, a swipe from right to left goes back to Home.
  • Tap beside the dots to turn one page to that side.
  • Tap the dots to open the overview with a picture of every page, then tap a picture. Or hold the dots, slide onto a picture and let go. The overview closes after 10 seconds.
A page: lights by room The overview of all pages

Title, icon, time, gear and overview can be changed or switched off in the Web Admin's Head bar tab.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
Every display has three layouts, each with its own places for the tiles:

Layout Look Head bar landscape Fewer, larger tiles under the head bar, with pages. New displays start with it. Head bar portrait The same for ESP32-P4 displays mounted upright. Classic The grid of earlier versions, with Settings and Back tiles and no head.

Switch the layout in the Web Admin's layout window; the display restarts with it. A new display that can stand upright asks for landscape or upright in its first-start setup.

Upright Upright, light theme 4-inch square display

docs.title: Light Theme
docs.text:
Choose Dark, Light or Automatic under Settings → Display → Theme or in the Web Admin. Automatic is light by day and dark at night. Filled tiles keep their color in both themes.

The light theme

docs.title: Edge Swipes
docs.text: Swipe inward from a screen edge for a quick action. Each edge can open Settings, go Home, go Back, or start the screensaver. New displays open Settings from the top edge and go Home from the bottom edge. Change the edges in the Web Admin's Global tab under Edge swipes.

docs.title: Folders
docs.text:
A folder tile opens its own page; its head shows the folder's name and the X returns. A protected folder asks for its PIN first; see Folder.

A page with the folders Security and Garage

docs.title: Popups
docs.text:
For tiles with detail controls, choose a tap or long press as the popup trigger in the Web Admin. The popup's head shows the tile's icon and circle, and most popups take the tile's color.

History popups have 7D and 24H views (Energy: 7D and Today); the previous data stays visible until the new period arrives. To read an earlier value, touch a graph and move your finger along it, or tap an Energy bar. The time and value appear above the graph, and the marker stays where you let go.

Tile Popup Sensor, Binary Sensor History graph or state timeline with Activity Number, Select, Date/Time Control above the history Energy Hourly and daily bars Switch Brightness, color, and color temperature for lights; on/off otherwise Cover Position and tilt Weather, Media, Climate Forecast, playback, temperature and modes Fan, Lock, Alarm Panel Speed and presets, lock and open, arming modes Camera Live video, also full screen Calendar Month with the day's events, or the coming weeks as a list

Home Assistant can also open a folder or popup using the display's View Select entity.

docs.title: Built-in Camera Indicator
docs.text: While Home Assistant uses the display's own built-in camera, a red line runs along the top edge. In the head bar layouts a camera circle with a red icon appears in the head; in the classic layout a Camera active pill appears below the line. Tap the circle or the pill to end the live stream; the camera stays available for the next request. Both parts can be switched off in the Web Admin.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The gear in the head opens Settings. If Settings is PIN-protected, enter the PIN first. Settings can also open by an edge swipe; the factory PIN 466384537 also unlocks protected folders, see Settings access.

Settings has four pages; the X closes it.

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
Brightness, sleep timeout, rotation, and the theme; for the screensaver its start time and brightness. Never switches the corresponding timeout off. Rotation offers 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° on displays that turn in quarter turns, 0° and 180° on the others. Tap a Clock tile to open the screensaver at once.

On displays with a speaker the page is called Display & Sound and adds a Sound group: the speaker volume and, where there is a microphone, its switch. Home Assistant sets the same values.

Display

docs.title: WiFi
docs.text:
The connected network with its address and Disconnect, the Hotspot for a setup without a network, and the networks around. Search looks again; tap a network to join it with its password. Displays with Ethernet can switch to it here.

WiFi

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
Choose English, German, French, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Spanish, or Russian, the time zone, the time and date formats, and the keyboard layout. Tile titles support Cyrillic characters in every text size.

The keyboard follows the language when set to Auto: German, Czech, and Slovak use QWERTZ, French uses AZERTY, Russian uses ЙЦУКЕН, and English, Polish, and Spanish use QWERTY. The key beside ?123 shows the language's own letters first, for example ä, ö, ü, and ß in German, á, č, ď, é, ě, í, ň, ó, ř, š, ť, ú, ů, ý, and ž in Czech, or ñ, á, é, í, ó, ú, ü, ¿, and ¡ in Spanish, followed by other common European letters; ABC returns to the letters. Holding a letter offers its accented forms, the language's own first. On the Russian keyboard the same key switches to QWERTY for passwords (ABC) and back (АБВ), and holding е or ь gives ё or ъ.

Localization

docs.title: System
docs.text:
System
  • Firmware: the version and the device; Update looks for a new release, see Firmware Updates.
  • Connection: Home Assistant with a check while the display is connected, and the way: Direct · Bridge with the Bridge's address, or MQTT · Broker.
  • Security: Pairing with Home Assistant (Installation): Pair while unpaired, Unpair inside Paired. Web Admin password: Allow lets you set the first password in the Web Admin within two minutes; while a password is set, you can remove a forgotten one here. Both ask before they act.
  • Setup opens the first-start setup again, Restart restarts the display, GitHub shows a QR code for the project.

docs.title: Connection & pairing
docs.text:
Display not found after Pair

  1. Tap Pair again under Settings → System → Security; Home Assistant can find the display for two minutes.
  2. Display and Home Assistant must be in the same network: Home Assistant finds the display by mDNS (zeroconf). VLANs, guest networks and Docker without host networking often block it. Then add the display by its IP address: tap Pair, then Add integration → HomeTiles Bridge → Panel by IP address (direct connection) (Bridge v0.9.4).
  3. Check that the HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.0 is installed and Home Assistant was restarted afterwards.
  4. Look under Settings → Devices & services for an existing HomeTiles Bridge entry of this display: a display that already has one shows Connect the panel instead of Panel found.

Paired, but no tile data

  1. Settings → System on the display should show Home Assistant: Connected. If not, allow TCP ports 8140–8147 from the display to the Home Assistant host.
  2. Without a Web Admin password, only the entities selected under HomeTiles Bridge → Configure → Entity configuration reach the display.
  3. A display on MQTT needs matching Device topic base and Home Assistant prefix on the display and in its Bridge entry.

See the Installation for first-time installation.

AP mode

The hotspot password is 12345678, also shown with a QR code. It switches off after 10 minutes without a saved configuration. The connection to Home Assistant and the Web Admin are unavailable while AP mode is active.

Home Assistant or MQTT is offline

The display keeps running and reconnects automatically when Home Assistant or the broker returns. Entity states resync after reconnection.

States arrive, but commands or updates fail

New values still appear, but lights do not react, the Web Admin does not load, or an OTA update stops partway. The Wi-Fi connection is stuck, and a restart from the menu may not clear it:

  1. Unplug the display for 10 seconds, then power it on again.
  2. If that does not help, restart the Wi-Fi router.

docs.title: Tiles & camera
docs.text:
No camera video

Camera tiles are experimental and require ESP32-P4, firmware v0.6.3 or newer, and Bridge v0.6.28 or newer.

  1. Update the Bridge through HACS and restart Home Assistant.
  2. Select the camera in the Bridge's Entity Configuration and verify it works in Home Assistant.
  3. Allow the display to reach the Home Assistant host on TCP ports 8124–8131.
  4. Check the Home Assistant log for FFmpeg or camera-source errors.

Snapshot cameras follow their source refresh rate. For a model-specific limitation or test build, open the status information in the device list.

Missing local I/O entity

Save the assignment in the panel's I/O tab. It should become selectable by tiles on that panel immediately. For Home Assistant, use Bridge v0.6.32 or newer and an MQTT connection; restart Home Assistant after updating the Bridge, then save the assignment again or use Pairing.

Empty Energy tile

Configure Home Assistant's Energy Dashboard and enable the matching electricity, gas, or water category in the Bridge options.

docs.title: Display behavior
docs.text:
Forgot the Settings or folder PIN

Enter the factory PIN 466384537 (HOMETILES on a phone keypad). It unlocks Settings and every protected folder; then change the PIN in the Web Admin. See Settings access.

ESP32-S3 briefly goes black while saving

The backlight pauses during flash writes to prevent a shifted image. It should recover immediately. If it stays black, report the failure with the exact model and serial log.

Waveshare briefly flashes blue while saving or updating

A brief blue flash is a known cosmetic limitation when flash writes interrupt display refresh.

Tab5 dims during AP startup or reboot

Temporary dimming reduces the power demand during WiFi startup. Your configured brightness returns when WiFi connects.

Faint images of previous content

LCD image retention can follow static, high-contrast content, especially on a cold panel. It normally fades; use a shorter display sleep timeout to reduce it.

docs.title: Updates & crashes
docs.text:
Black screen or MQTT disconnect during an update

Expected: a Web Admin upload turns off the display, and installation temporarily disconnects MQTT. The device restarts and reconnects afterwards. Keep it powered until the update finishes.

Update check fails or shows no new version

Restart the display and check again. Compare the version under Settings → System with the latest release.

Update download repeatedly fails

Use the Web Admin upload with the matching plain .bin, not _factory.bin, or use the online flasher in Update mode.

Unexpected restart, crash, or network freeze

  1. Open Screenshot & Diagnostics in the Web Admin and select Download crash log.
  2. If a core dump is available, download it and put the .bin in a .zip for GitHub.
  3. For live output or a restart loop, use the browser Device logs viewer and copy the serial log.
  4. Open an issue with the exact model, firmware version, action that triggered the problem, and logs.

A core dump can contain tile names, entity data, and other working memory. Share only the crash log if you prefer. Check the device status for known issues and available fixes.

docs.title: Flashing the Firmware
docs.text: Open the online flasher, or use the short manual flashing alternative.

docs.title: Local Hardware I/O
docs.text:
Use up to eight available GPIOs for switches or DS18B20 temperature inputs. These work locally, including when Home Assistant or MQTT is offline.

Open I/O in the Web Admin. Assignments belong to the physical panel and are excluded from dashboard exports.

I/O tab with a switch output

docs.title: Switch Outputs
docs.text:
1. Select + Switch and enter a name.
  2. Choose an offered GPIO.
  3. Set the active High / Low level where configurable.
  4. Choose the startup state, Off / On.
  5. Select Save to apply the assignment. Restart reboots separately and does not save edits.

For the 86-Panel-ETH-2RO, select Relay 1 or Relay 2 explicitly; the shared Waveshare 4B firmware also serves boards without these relays. On closes NO-COM, Off closes COM-NC, and their active-high polarity is fixed.

Relay-equipped Guition ESP32-4848S040 variants expose their first onboard relay. The Golden Security GS-T3E v2 offers the two relays every published variant has, on GPIO45 and GPIO46.

docs.title: DS18B20 Temperature Inputs
docs.text:
Select + Temperature, enter a name, choose a GPIO and precision, then save.

Use one DS18B20 per GPIO, external sensor power, and a 4.7 kΩ pull-up from data to 3.3 V. The internal pull-up is disabled. Values are available to local Sensor tiles on the dashboard and screensaver.

docs.title: Tiles And Home Assistant
docs.text:
After saving, select the local entity in a Switch or Sensor tile on the same panel.

Bridge v0.6.32 or newer also adds it to the panel's Home Assistant device. Outputs become switch entities; temperatures become sensor entities. Existing names changed manually in Home Assistant are preserved.

docs.title: Available Pins
docs.text:
The I/O selector offers only pins assigned for use by that device's firmware profile. Check connected expansion modules for conflicts; some listed profiles still need physical I/O validation.

86 Panel relays GPIO 32 and 46 P3 schematic-derived; onboard relays only for the exact 86-Panel-ETH-2RO Waveshare Touch LCD 4.3 inch None The exact board profile reserves its documented display, touch, microSD, USB and ESP-Hosted connections Waveshare Touch LCD 5 inch None The exact board profile reserves its documented display, touch, audio, microSD, USB and ESP-Hosted connections;
