verify attached hardware Waveshare 10.1 inch GPIO 2, 3, 4, 5, 21, 22, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52 Physical hardware validation needed Guition JC8012P4A1 Expansion FPC GPIO 2, 3, 4, 5, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 45, 46, 47, 48 Schematic-derived; verify the connected expansion board Guition JC8012P4A1 V2 Expansion FPC GPIO 2, 3, 4, 5, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 45, 46, 47, 48 Separate V2 profile; same reported board wiring, community validation ongoing Guition JC1060P470C V1 / V2 Expand GPIO 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 20, 32, 33, 46, 47 GPIO45 is reserved for the active-low SD-card power switch; physical validation needed Guition JC4880P443 None The exact board profile reserves its documented display, touch, microSD, USB and ESP-Hosted connections; contributor-tested Guition ESP32-4848S040 Onboard Relay 1 on GPIO 40 for relay-equipped variants Supported; relay-equipped variants only Golden Security GS-T3E v2 Onboard relays on GPIO 45 and 46 From openHASP and ESPHome configurations; the variant-specific third and fourth relays are not offered; community validation pending Waveshare 7B / 7B-C None No configurable GPIOs in these profiles Waveshare S3 LCD-4 Rev 4.0 / S3 LCD-4B None No configurable GPIOs in these profiles

3.3 V logic only

Never connect a relay coil, mains voltage, or another high-current load directly to an ESP32 GPIO. Use a 3.3 V-compatible driver or relay module and follow the manufacturer's schematic. Do not assign a pin already used by an attached module.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The setup with Home Assistant is now part of the Installation.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Manual flashing, no HACS, an MQTT broker or an older display: Advanced setup. Problems: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Flash the firmware
docs.text:
Connect the display by USB to a computer with Chrome or Edge and choose your exact device.

Firmware

Choose the published release or a local HomeTiles .bin file.

Loading published release... Local HomeTiles .bin file Device

Select the exact model printed on the device or rear label.

Loading devices... Mode

Update keeps settings. First install / factory reset erases all local data.

Update First install / factory reset Check

Confirm the exact label before connecting the serial port.

I checked the exact model label. Erase all settings and local data. Flash

Keep power, USB and this tab open while flashing.

Connect and flash Loading...

Log capture is active. Selecting a port with Connect and flash stops capture and releases its USB port. Cancelling the port selection keeps capture running.

Preparing 0% Flash log Copy log Clear log

docs.title: Install the Bridge
docs.text: Add the HomeTiles Bridge to Home Assistant with the button, select Download and restart Home Assistant.

docs.title: Set up the display
docs.text:
The display guides you. At Pair, select Add in Home Assistant under Settings → Devices & services and confirm the same number on both sides.

1. On the display: tap Pair 2. In Home Assistant: Add 3. Same number: Numbers match: connect 4. On the display: Confirm

docs.title: Add your tiles
docs.text: Open the address the display shows in your computer's browser and build your dashboard in the Web Admin.

docs.title: Screensaver
docs.text:
Create a separate layout with a clock, tiles, and an optional image slideshow or a picture from Home Assistant in the Web Admin's Screensaver tab.

Screensaver with clock and sensor tiles

docs.title: Open It Manually or Automatically
docs.text:
• Tap a Clock tile to open it immediately.
  • Set an inactivity timeout under Settings → Display → Screensaver. Never disables automatic activation.
  • Use Screensaver Brightness for separate screensaver brightness; the display previews the level while you drag.
  • Tap free background space to return to the dashboard.
Display and screensaver settings

docs.title: Prepare the microSD Card
docs.text:
A slideshow needs microSD support. The Waveshare S3 LCD-4 Rev 4.0 and S3 LCD-4B profiles cannot use SD images. The clock and tiles work on a black background without a card. A picture from Home Assistant needs no card.

  1. Format the card as FAT32 and insert it.
  2. Create an images folder in the card's root (/images).
  3. Copy your JPEGs there, or upload them with the Web Admin file manager.
  4. Open the Screensaver tab. New images are added to the list, and deleted files disappear from it.

docs.title: Image Requirements
docs.text:
• Export baseline (non-progressive) JPEG, with a .jpg or .jpeg extension.
  • Use RGB/sRGB, not CMYK.
  • Resize to your display's resolution in the device list. For a shared image set, keep the longest edge at 1920 pixels or less.
  • Use quality 80–90 and keep each file below 8 MB.

If an image stays black, re-export it at the display's native size with these settings. A large camera photo or progressive JPEG may fail even if the filename ends in .jpg.

docs.title: Configure the Slideshow
docs.text:
In the Web Admin's Screensaver tab, click the background.

Screensaver editor Setting What it does Use images Enable the slideshow instead of a black background Shuffle Choose images randomly Tile shadows / Tile borders Style the overlay tiles Image checkboxes Include or exclude files Arrow buttons Change the image order Duration Display time for every image Zoom Enlarge the selected image Focus X / Focus Y Move its crop horizontally or vertically

Changes save automatically.

docs.title: Picture from Home Assistant
docs.text:
Instead of the slideshow, the screensaver can show the picture of a Home Assistant image or camera entity, for example a weather webcam.

  1. Connect the panel to the Bridge directly (pairing on the panel); panels on MQTT keep the slideshow.
  2. Release the entity in the Bridge options under Images (screensaver). A camera released under Cameras works too.
  3. In the Screensaver tab, click the background, set Type to Picture from Home Assistant, keep Use images on, and choose the entity.
Type: Picture from Home Assistant

A new picture of an image entity appears at once. A camera sends a new still image at the interval set under Refresh (s), 3 to 60 seconds, and only while the screensaver is visible. Scaling sets how the picture uses the screen:

Scaling What it does Fill Covers the whole screen; what stands out is cut off Fit The whole picture as large as possible, black bars where needed Original A smaller picture at its own size in the middle; a larger one like Fit

QR codes and maps are enlarged with sharp edges. Upright displays get the picture in their upright size. Switch back to Slideshow (SD card) at any time; the slideshow settings stay stored.

docs.title: Position the Clock
docs.text: Select the clock to change its time/date formats, font sizes, alignment, and shadow. Drag it anywhere and resize its text area; it is independent of the tile grid.

docs.title: Add Tiles
docs.text:
The bottom two rows support Sensor, Binary Sensor, Energy, Switch, Button, and Media tiles. Select a slot, choose its type, and move or resize it as on the dashboard. Adjust Color and Opacity together.

States stay live. Popups do not open in screensaver mode. Local I/O switches and temperatures remain available when Home Assistant is offline.

Media tiles need at least 2×2 cells. Cover art can slow entry and slide changes; use fewer Media tiles if the slideshow feels slow.

docs.title: Backup and Restore
docs.text: Web Admin Export includes the screensaver layout and settings. Image files stay on the microSD card and must be copied separately.

docs.title: Tile Types
docs.text:
Create and configure tiles in the Web Admin and choose their entity in the entity picker.

Home Assistant tiles show entity data or control your devices. Local tiles provide clocks, text, folders, animations, and spacing.

All tiles share title, icon, color, size, and position settings. For types with a popup, choose whether a tap or long press opens it; the popup takes on the tile's icon, circle, and color. See On-Device UI for how popups behave.

Press Enter in the title field for a second line. The two lines share the same vertical center as a single-line title; text that does not fit ends in .... The display, popup header, and Web Admin preview use the same title.

Sizes: every tile resizes in half steps from 1×1. All tiles except Weather, Media, and Animation can also be half a cell high; they then show the title and state or value next to the icon, without a bar.

Sensor Switch Number

Colors: a tile's color always comes from its icon: the icon's own color, the color of a light, or the color you pick for the icon. Fill fills the tile with that color. Rules color the icon by an entity's value or state, and a rule row with Fill fills the tile while it matches. Clock, Text and Animation tiles have their own color, and Clock and Text tiles can be Transparent.

docs.title: Home Assistant Tiles
docs.text: These types show or control a Home Assistant entity.

docs.title: Sensor
docs.text:
Shows a numeric or text-valued sensor.* entity. Configure the unit, decimals, and value size. Display mode adds a gauge, a graph of the last 24 hours, a bar, an arc, or a ring below the header with a minimum and maximum: filled, as a line, or striped, with the value in the header or inside the arc or ring.

Icon color With Fill Popup, 24 hours Graph Stripes Striped arc

Popup: the current value in the header and its history: a graph for numbers with 30D, 7D, 24H, 6H, and 1H, or a timeline and Activity list for text states with 7D or 24H. The 30D and 1H ranges need HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.6 or newer. Touch the graph and move your finger to read an earlier value; the time and value appear above the graph, and the marker stays where you let go.

A local DS18B20 input can also supply the value without Home Assistant; local inputs have no Home Assistant history popup.

docs.title: Binary Sensor
docs.text:
Shows a binary_sensor.* entity with the matching state and icon, such as Open/Closed or Motion/Clear. Unknown and unavailable states are shown separately.

Tile Popup

Popup: a 7D or 24H state timeline and Activity list.

docs.title: Number
docs.text:
Changes a number.* or input_number.* entity. The tile shows its current value and unit; the popup uses the minimum, maximum, step, and input mode supplied by Home Assistant.

Tile Popup
  • Slider values use a centered slider with the value above it. Release the slider to send the final value.
  • Temperatures use − / value / +, like the Climate target control.
  • Other box-mode values use a bounded roller or step buttons, depending on their range.

Popup: the control above a numeric history graph and Activity for 7D or 24H. History requires the entity to be recorded by Home Assistant.

docs.title: Select
docs.text:
Changes a select.* or input_select.* entity using its current Home Assistant options. The tile shows the selected value; the popup uses the same dropdown interaction as Settings.

Tile Popup

Popup: the dropdown above a compact timeline and Activity for 7D or 24H. An unavailable entity or incomplete option list disables selection. To operate another display's view, choose that display's View entity.

docs.title: Date/Time
docs.text:
Changes time.*, date.*, datetime.*, or input_datetime.* entities. Available controls follow whether the entity contains a time, a date, or both.

Tile Popup

Time uses a single visible row of large, swipeable hh / mm / ss values, with wraparound between 23 and 00 or 59 and 00. Date fields use step controls without a keyboard.

Popup: the controls above Activity for 7D or 24H. Home Assistant's time zone is used for date/time commands.

Slider edits are sent on release; step and time edits are grouped after a short pause, and the display keeps your edit while a slow device confirms it. Unavailable entities cannot be changed.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Shows Home Assistant Energy Dashboard statistics for electricity, gas, water, or cost. Enable the matching Bridge energy category. Configure the energy entity, unit, decimals, and value size. Display mode: Graph shows today's hours as bars below the header.

Tile Half height Graph Popup, today Popup, 7 days

Popup: Year (a bar per month), Month and Week (a bar per day), and Today (a bar per hour), each from its start up to now. The week starts on the day chosen under Web Admin → Localization → First day of the week. Tap a bar to read its time and value; a dot marks the bar you read. Year and Week need HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.6 or newer.

docs.title: Power Flow
docs.text:
Shows the power of the solar panels, the grid, a battery, and the home as nodes, with dots that move along the lines in the direction the power flows and faster when more power flows. Choose a power sensor for each node; a node without a sensor stays hidden. Invert sign turns around a grid or battery sensor that counts the other way, and a battery charge sensor adds its level to the battery node. Show title and icon adds the tile header, and Show card draws the tile's card behind the nodes.

Battery to home

Tap a node to open its sensor's popup.

docs.title: Switch
docs.text:
Toggles a compatible entity and reflects its state. Choose the entity, Layout, and popup trigger.

Layout Tile Automatic A dimmer bar for lights that can dim, otherwise the switch bar. Default for new tiles. Dimmer A brightness bar across the tile: press or drag to set the level, like the popup's brightness slider. Lights without dimming get the switch bar. Switch An on/off bar with a thumb, like the popup's switch. Icon button No bar: tap the tile to toggle.

Orientation: Horizontal lays the bar across the tile; Upright stands it up next to the header, the dimmer filling from the bottom and the switch on at the top.

The tile shows the state (On, Off, or the brightness) under its title. Half-height tiles show the state only; tap toggles, and the other gesture opens the popup. Commands while dragging are paced like Home Assistant, and the last level is always sent. A light fills its tile in its own color.

Dimmer Dimmer, colored light Switch Switch, off Icon button Home Assistant domain Tile action switch, light Turn on/off input_boolean Set a Toggle helper on/off automation Enable/disable the automation's triggers fan, humidifier, remote, siren Turn the entity on/off using its configured defaults

Fan and Siren controls require both HA on/off feature flags. Missing, unavailable, or unsupported entities cannot be operated.

An automation switch enables/disables the automation; it does not run its actions immediately. Turning it off follows HA's default behavior and stops running actions. For fan speed, presets, and direction use the Fan tile; humidity, remote commands/activities, and siren tones are outside this tile's on/off controls.

Local outputs and relays appear in the same selector and work without Home Assistant.

Popup for lights: brightness, color, and color temperature; only the controls the light supports appear. The bottom icons switch views, and the power button toggles the light.

Brightness Color Color temperature

Popup for other compatible entities: the on/off slider in the same popup.

docs.title: Cover
docs.text:
Controls a cover entity and shows its state and position when available.

Tile Popup

The tile shows the position as a bar, like the Switch dimmer; half-height tiles show the state only. While the cover opens or closes, its arrow pulses.

Popup: separate position and tilt sliders, or open, close, and stop buttons. Controls depend on the cover's capabilities and availability. A slider sends its position once on release, like Home Assistant, and then follows the reported position.

docs.title: Button
docs.text:
Runs a scene, script or button with a tap; there is no popup. Its picker finds every scene, script and button through the Bridge, like the other tiles. Before v0.9.2 this tile was called Scene; existing tiles keep working.

Button Button Button Home Assistant domain Tile action scene Activate the scene (scene.turn_on) script Start the script without additional fields (script.turn_on) button Press the button once (button.press) input_button Press the Button helper once (input_button.press)

A never-pressed button remains usable even when HA reports an unknown timestamp. Missing or unavailable actions are ignored. Existing aliases remain stable when you reorder the selection or add entities with the same object name; custom aliases remain supported.

Use an HA script with defaults when an action needs parameters. Read-only binary_sensor and event entities cannot be pressed or switched. Locks, alarm panels, and fans have their own tiles; vacuums, valves, and update entities have different actions and are not mapped to these tile types; Cover, Climate, and Media keep their dedicated tiles.

docs.title: Weather
docs.text:
Shows current conditions and the next days from a weather entity. The number of days follows the tile's width.

Tile Popup, next days Popup, by hour

Popup: temperatures, precipitation, and rain probability for the next days or by hour. Use the arrows to browse the available forecast.

Icons: weather icons are filled and colored (sun gold, clouds grey, rain blue, snow ice blue, thunderstorms purple, wind teal, night grey blue). Turn off Colored weather icons in the tile settings to keep the white outlines. With Fill, the tile takes the color of the current weather; an icon color you set yourself draws the whole icon in that color. When the Bridge sends sunrise and sunset, partly cloudy and clear hours after sunset show the moon.

Own sensors: choose a Temperature sensor to show your own outdoor sensor instead of the weather entity's current temperature, and a Humidity sensor to add its humidity, as in 21.5 °C · 64 %. The tile and the popup header use them, in the weather entity's unit; the forecast still comes from the weather entity. A chosen sensor without a numeric state shows --.

docs.title: Media
docs.text:
Shows cover art, title, and playback controls for a media_player entity. Media tiles need at least 2×2 cells. With From cover, the icon and the tile take the color of the cover art. The icon shows whether the player plays, pauses or is off (for example speaker-play), and while a song plays or pauses, bars stand over its title and move while it plays.

Tile Popup

Popup: cover art with title, artist and album, the time bar, playback controls and volume. Popup in the Web Admin chooses Cover left or Cover centered. The popup shows only the controls the player offers in Home Assistant; shuffle and repeat take the icon's color and a dot when they are on. The time follows the position Home Assistant reports.

The ⋯ button in the bottom right corner opens a menu with up to three lists, each where the player offers it:

  • Speakers: play on several speakers together. The button shows how many play together.
  • Source: the player's sources and sound modes.
  • Library: browse Home Assistant's media for the player and start a title, album or playlist. The library keeps its place until the popup closes.

The menu and the library need HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.4 or newer.

Speakers Library

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Controls a climate entity. The icon and accent indicate active heating, cooling, drying, or fan operation.

Configure mini-tiles for temperatures, humidity, targets, and mode, or choose Automatic. Arrange them in the Climate mini-tile editor. A small tile with only the target shows the mode and room temperature in its head and the target between − and +.

Heating Cooling

Popup: adjust the target with the dial or plus/minus buttons. Available controls may include heating/cooling targets, humidity, mode, presets, fan, and swing; longer option lists scroll.

Popup

docs.title: Fan
docs.text:
Controls a fan entity.

The tile shows the state and speed. Its bar sets the speed: stepless like the Switch dimmer, in segments for fans with only a few speeds, or as an on/off switch for fans without speed control. Orientation: Upright stands the bar up like the Switch tile's, the speeds stacking from the bottom. Tap or long press, whichever does not open the popup, switches the fan on or off.

On Off Popup

Popup: the speed above a large slider, and below it the power button and, when the fan supports them, preset, oscillation, and direction. Only the controls the fan reports appear.

Presets

docs.title: Lock
docs.text:
Controls a lock entity.

The tile shows the state in Home Assistant's colors: green while locked, red while unlocked, open, or jammed, orange while locking or unlocking. Its bar locks and unlocks; when the state is unknown or jammed it shows separate Unlock and Lock buttons.

Locked Unlocked Popup

Popup: a switch (up = locked) and, for locks that can open the door, Open door with a second tap to confirm. When Home Assistant needs a code, the code entry opens first.

Code entry

docs.title: Alarm Panel
docs.text:
Controls an alarm_control_panel entity.

The tile shows the state in Home Assistant's colors: green while armed, orange while arming, pending, or disarming, red when triggered, grey while disarmed. Its bar holds Disarm and the arming modes that fit.

Armed Triggered

Popup: the modes the panel supports (Home, Away, Night, Vacation, Custom) and Disarm. While the panel arms, waits, disarms, or is triggered, only Disarm remains. When Home Assistant needs a code, the code entry opens first.

Popup Code entry Triggered

Lock and Alarm Panel security: both run commands only on a paired display with a Web Admin password; otherwise the tile and popup say what is missing. Home Assistant checks every code as in its own UI; unlocking, opening, and disarming always need the entity's code. A device without its own code can only be unlocked, opened, or disarmed when it is listed under Allow opening without a code in the Bridge options. For devices that ignore a wrong code, enter their codes under Codes for locks and alarm panels so the Bridge checks them; after five wrong codes, code entry is blocked for a while. Numeric codes are supported; devices that need a text code must be operated in Home Assistant.

Lock and Alarm Panel tiles show only states the device reports: a command waits with the icon pulsing, and the popup says so when the device does not answer. They are not available on the screensaver.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
Shows a camera or image entity. The camera can also be the built-in camera of another HomeTiles display.

  • Show: the icon, or the Picture: the tile shows the camera's current image in its own size, with the title in a pill. Circle and title can be Automatic, Dark or Light, with an adjustable transparency.
  • Tap opens: the Popup with a 16:9 live video, or the Full screen video at once.
Tile with its picture Popup with a live image

ESP32-P4 displays play the video at up to 30 frames per second, in the popup and full screen; ESP32-S3 displays at about 4. Allow local TCP access to the Home Assistant host on ports 8124–8131. See Camera connection for requirements and performance notes. A doorbell automation can open a camera full screen with the display's View entity.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
Shows up to four calendar entities, each in its own color (blue, teal, purple, orange, in the order of the calendar fields). Requires a Bridge with calendar support; select the calendars under Calendars in the Bridge options.

What the tile shows depends on its size and View:

  • Half height: the next event: "Next · 10:00" above its title ("Now" while it runs). Two cells wide, the top line counts down ("Next · in 1 h 30 min") and the start time follows the title.
  • Half height, View Today: "Today" above the number of events left today ("3 events", "No events").
  • 1×1: a countdown: the next event's title at the top, its day large in the middle ("Today", "Tomorrow", "Monday") and how far away it is below ("in 1 h 30 min", "in 2 days").
  • Two cells wide, one row: Up next: the event running now or the next one, with its time and a countdown.
  • Two rows or more: the agenda: the coming days with their events; all-day events first.
  • Week: a dot per calendar with events and today's column tinted. One row high, the strip shows the seven days from today; taller, the week from its first day.
  • Month: the month grid with today and a dot per calendar. Only on displays larger than 480×480 and on tiles of at least 2×2; elsewhere the tile shows the agenda.

Week starts on: Automatic follows Web Admin → Localization → First day of the week, whose own Automatic follows the display language (Sunday in English, Monday otherwise); or choose Monday, Sunday, or Saturday for this tile. The tile and its popup use it.

Popup: with two or more calendars, their names and colors on top; then the month with a dot per calendar; tap a day to see its events below. List shows the coming four weeks instead. The arrows move by month (or week in the list) as far as the Bridge sent events, and Today jumps back.

The display shows the events in Home Assistant's time zone. Events edited in Home Assistant appear within 15 minutes; an event that starts or ends updates the tile at once.

docs.title: Vacuum
docs.text:
Controls a vacuum entity. Requires HomeTiles Bridge v0.9.7 or newer; select the vacuums under Vacuums in the Bridge options.

  • Half height: the name and the state with the battery.
  • One row: the name and the state ("Docked · 84 %") beside the icon, the buttons below: Clean (Pause while cleaning) on one column, Clean and Dock on two, Clean, Stop and Dock from three columns. From 1.5 rows the state stands in the middle.
  • Two columns and two rows or more: the map on the left, the state, battery and cleaned area beside it, the buttons below.

Only the buttons the vacuum supports are active.

Map: Automatic takes the image or camera entity of the vacuum's device; or choose one. Refresh (s) sets how often a camera map is fetched (3 to 60 seconds); an image entity sends a new map when it changes.

Popup: the map (Map left or Map centre), cleaned area, cleaning time and battery, Clean, Stop and Dock, and a menu (⋯) with the suction power, the rooms to clean and Locate. Rooms are the Home Assistant areas mapped to the vacuum; they need Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer and the area mapping in the vacuum's entity settings.

docs.title: Local Tiles
docs.text: These types work without Home Assistant.

docs.title: Clock
docs.text:
Shows the time and date. Choose the style (Digital, Analog or Wall clock), the weekday, the date format, the alignment and rolling digits; the formats follow the display's localization unless you set them per tile. Tap a clock to open the screensaver.

Digital Analog, transparent Wall clock

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
A label with a selectable font size, aligned left, centered or right and top, middle or bottom. It can be half a cell high and Transparent, for example as a heading above a group of tiles, as on the Lights page.

Text

docs.title: Folder
docs.text:
Opens a sub-page with its own grid. In the head bar layouts its head has an X to go back; the classic layout adds a back tile. A folder on Home can also become a page. See Folders for setup and optional PIN protection.

Folder Folder Protected folder

A folder tile can follow an entity inside it: with rules and Entity color, a Climate folder turns orange while heating and blue while cooling.

A protected folder asks for its PIN before it opens. The PIN pad takes the folder tile's color and shows the folder's name with the state Locked; below Enter PIN, one dot appears per typed digit. The PIN has 4 to 8 digits.

PIN entry

docs.title: Animation
docs.text: Plays a .panim pixel animation from /animations on microSD. Configure frame rate, fit, and zoom.

docs.title: Empty
docs.text: Leaves an empty cell for spacing.

docs.title: Firmware Updates
docs.text: Normal updates keep your Wi-Fi, the connection to Home Assistant and your dashboard. Keep the display powered until installation finishes, then check the version under Settings → System.

docs.title: On-device updater
docs.text:
Open Settings → System, tap Update, and install the offered version. The display restarts when finished; Web Admin and the connection to Home Assistant come back automatically.

Settings → System with Update

docs.title: Web Admin upload
docs.text:
Use this method for a local test build or when downloading directly on the display fails.

  1. Download the exact model's plain .bin from the release page. Do not select _factory.bin.
  2. Open http://<display-ip>/ and find Firmware.
  3. Choose the file and start the upload. The screen may go black during installation; wait for the display to restart.
Firmware update in the Web Admin

Check exact model, revision and known limitations in the device list. The Web Admin can also run the same release check as the display.

docs.title: USB update
docs.text:
If the display is unreachable over the network, open the online flasher and choose Update. It preserves local settings and writes only to the inactive application slot.

For a new device or an intentional full reset, use First install / factory reset there instead. This erases all local data.

docs.title: Going back to v0.8.0
docs.text:
The display only offers newer versions, but you can install v0.8.0 with the Web Admin upload. v0.8.0 only knows the classic layout. Prepare the panel first:

  1. Back up: use Export in the Web Admin and keep the file.
  2. Switch to Classic: click the Layout field in the Global tab, choose Classic, make sure no tile is red, save, and switch the panel to it. The panel now shows what v0.8.0 will show.
  3. Upload the model's plain v0.8.0 .bin in the Web Admin.

Panels mounted upright show the classic landscape layout on v0.8.0. Head bar layouts, pages, the light theme and the other new settings stay stored; v0.8.0 ignores them, and they return when you update to v0.9.0 again.

v0.8.0 has no direct link to the Bridge and needs MQTT. A panel that uses the direct link needs its MQTT broker in the Web Admin again, and in Home Assistant delete its linked HomeTiles Bridge entry and add the panel again over MQTT.

docs.title: Going back to v0.6.x
docs.text:
The display only offers newer versions, but you can install an older release with the Web Admin upload. v0.6.x does not know half-size tiles: a half tile appears at whole size and can overlap its neighbor. Prepare the dashboard first:

  1. Back up: use Export in the Web Admin and keep the file.
  2. Make every tile whole: give every tile a whole position and size (no 0.5 values), and arrange the tiles so they do not overlap. This includes back tiles in folders, Climate tiles with a height of 1.5, and the tiles in the screensaver.
  3. Upload the older model's plain .bin in the Web Admin.

Colors, rules, icon circles, the tile radius, and camera settings need no preparation. v0.6.x ignores them, and they return when you update to v0.7.0 again, as long as the tiles keep their places in between.

An export that contains half-size tiles cannot be imported in v0.6.x. Export again after step 2 if you want a file for the older version.

docs.title: If an update fails
docs.text:
Restart the display and retry once. If a direct GitHub download still fails, use the Web Admin upload above. The updater may restart more than once during recovery; check the installed version afterwards. An interrupted normal update leaves the previously selected application bootable.

If it still fails, download the diagnostics and report the problem. For the Guition JC8012 V1 Camera/Web OTA fix, see its note in the device list.

To build your own firmware, follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Web Admin Panel
docs.text:
Open http://<display-ip>/ in your computer's browser to edit your dashboard. The display shows the address in the last step of its setup and under Settings → WiFi; Home Assistant shows it on the display's device page.

Web Admin dashboard editor

Select a tile in the preview to open its settings. Each folder has its own tab, and the preview shows the display's current layout.

Changes save automatically

Tile edits save as you make them and appear on the display.

docs.title: Creating a Tile
docs.text:
1. Click an empty cell.
  2. Choose a Type.
  3. Choose the entity where needed and adjust the tile.

The entity picker searches like Home Assistant: type part of a name, an area or a device. Favorites puts this display's entities on top (those its tiles use and those selected for it in the Bridge), Recent the ones you picked most in this browser, and All lists everything that fits the tile. A paired display with a Web Admin password finds every entity in Home Assistant; otherwise the picker offers the entities selected in the Bridge options. Picking an entity also takes its name and icon.

Every tile has these settings:

  • Title: optional label; press Enter for a second line. Both lines are centered together, and each line ends in ... if it exceeds the available width.
  • Icon (MDI): a Material Design Icon name. Show icon list opens the catalog.
  • Color: the Icon color, and Fill to fill the tile with it. Without your own color the icon keeps the color of its entity, for example a light's color. Clock, Text and Animation tiles have their own color instead.
  • Advanced: options of the tile type, where it has any.
  • Column, Row, Width, Height: position and size in half steps.

See Tile Types to choose the right type.

The entity picker

docs.title: Type-specific settings
docs.text:
Fields depend on the selected type. A numeric Sensor offers:

Field Purpose Entity Sensor to display Unit Unit label, such as °C or W Decimals Decimal places Value size Size of the displayed value Display mode Text or a gauge with a minimum and maximum

Number, Select, and Date/Time also offer Value size with the same choices as Sensor. In half-height tiles the value uses 20, 24, or 28. Choose the matching entity and whether a tap or long press opens its popup.

Sensor tile settings

docs.title: Global Settings
docs.text:
The Global tab next to Tile applies to the whole display:

Setting What it does Tile borders Draws a thin line around the tiles. Clock and Text tiles can switch it off individually. Layout Shows the active layout and its grid; a click opens the layout window. Theme Dark, Light or Automatic (light by day, dark at night), for the display and the Web Admin. Edge swipes One action per screen edge: Settings, Home, Back, or the screensaver. New displays open Settings from the top and go Home from the bottom.

Corners, circles and the tile cards follow the theme; there is no separate radius or tile color setting.

The Global tab

docs.title: Head Bar
docs.text:
In the head bar layouts the Head bar tab, between Tile and Global, sets Home's head:

  • Home title and icon: Auto shows "Home" in the display's language and the house.
  • Gear for Settings, Clock, and Page overview on the dots. Without the overview, the dots only show the page.
The Head bar tab

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
Every display keeps its tiles in three layouts: Classic, Head bar landscape and Head bar portrait (portrait only on ESP32-P4 displays that can stand upright). A click on the Layout field in the Global tab opens the layout window (Change layout):

  • The screen is at the top left, the Storage to the right and below it. Drag tiles between them; a tile in the storage is not shown in that layout but keeps its settings.
  • Each folder has room for its storage on top of its grid cells, so tiles in the storage never take the place a new tile on a free cell needs. When a layout's storage holds more tiles than it has room for, Save waits until you place or delete some.
  • A folder that is completely full still shows the frame on a free cell; a click on it tells you so. Clear out the storage here and save.
  • Each layout has its own tab and places. Copy from … takes the places of another layout as a start.
  • A red tile has no place yet. While a folder or the Settings tile is red, Save and Switch wait: every folder must stay reachable.
  • X on a tile deletes it from every layout, after a question.
  • Switch restarts the display in the chosen layout. Its places stay saved when you switch back.
  • The Screensaver tab places the screensaver's tiles and clock for this layout.

Places are saved with Save; nothing changes on the display before that.

The layout window The same tiles placed for the upright layout

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
In the head bar layouts, Home has five page fields beside or below its grid. Drag a folder tile from Home into a field: the folder becomes a page and its tile leaves Home. Drag it out again to make it a tile. A new folder can go straight into a free field: select the field's + to create a page there. Pages have no PIN: a protected folder asks before its PIN is removed.

On the display, the page dots show the pages in the order of the fields.

Three folders as pages, and the Settings field

docs.title: Colors and Rules
docs.text:
A tile's color comes from its icon. Rules change the icon color while an entity has a matching state. Set Rules to On in the tile settings; a tile with its own entity starts at Own entity and Own rules:

  • Own entity / Other entity: follow the tile's own entity or any other entity. Button, Folder, Camera, Clock, and Text tiles have no entity of their own and always use another entity.
  • Entity color: use the color the entity shows itself: a light's color, heating or cooling on a climate entity, and the state colors of switches, covers, and binary sensors.
  • Own rules: choose the colors yourself, by value or by state (see below).

While a rule matches, it wins. Otherwise the settings above apply. Without a state, for example while Home Assistant is offline, the tile keeps its icon color.

Every color in a rule can also bring its own icon: the icon button next to a state row's color, or below a marker's value, picks it. While the rule matches, that icon replaces the tile's icon, in the tile and in its popup header; afterwards the tile's own icon comes back.

docs.title: Icon Color by Value
docs.text:
For Sensor, Energy, and Number tiles: a color bar between Min and Max. Smooth blends the colors, Steps changes at each marker. Start from Cold → Warm, Traffic light, Battery, Humidity, or Single color. Drag a marker to move it, click it to choose its color, and double-click the bar to add one (up to six). The tile's Fill fills it in the current color.

A battery from red to green

docs.title: Icon Color by State
docs.text:
For Sensor, Binary Sensor, Select, and Date/Time tiles: up to six states, each with a color. A row matches the exact state, or any state containing its text when contains is ticked; upper and lower case do not matter, and the first match wins. Binary sensors have one color for On and one for Off. Unavailable states keep the default color.

Each row has its own Fill: the tile is filled only while that row matches, and stays a plain card otherwise. In this example, a waste sensor says when to put the bin out. Its row for "Today" colors the icon orange and fills the tile, so only the bin that goes out today stands out.

State rules "Today": filled

docs.title: Editing Climate Mini-Tiles
docs.text:
Click a Climate mini-tile in the preview to edit it, or drag it to another slot. The outline shows whether you are selecting the parent tile or a mini-tile.

Choose temperature, humidity, targets, or mode. Automatic chooses values supported by the entity. Target is the single target temperature; Heating target and Cooling target are the two limits of devices that keep a range in Heat/Cool mode.

Resizing the parent changes the available slots. Mini-tiles that still fit keep their place; only those without room are hidden until the tile grows again.

Climate tile and mini-tile editor

docs.title: Moving, Resizing, Copying
docs.text:
• Move: drag a tile to another cell.
  • Resize: drag its edge handles or enter Width / Height. Sizes change in half steps; almost every tile can also be half a cell high.
  • Copy / Paste: duplicate a tile, including between folders. Paste onto an empty cell where the copied size fits.
  • Delete: clear a tile back to an empty cell.

docs.title: Folders
docs.text:
Choose the Folder type to create a sub-page. It appears as a Web Admin tab. In the head bar layouts its head has an X to go back; the classic layout adds a back tile. A folder that still contains tiles keeps its type until you empty it.

Delete Folder / Tab removes the folder and its tiles.

To protect a folder, select its tile, enable Protect this folder with a PIN, enter 4–8 digits, and press Apply PIN. The display then asks for the PIN before opening the folder. Folder PINs are stored only on that display and are excluded from exports.

A folder tile can also show the state of what is inside: with Rules → On, the climate entity and Entity color, a Climate folder turns orange while heating and blue while cooling.

In the classic layout, select the back tile to change its icon and color. It can be moved like any tile and made half a cell high.

docs.title: Settings Tile and Access
docs.text:
Settings opens from the gear in the head, from the Settings tile, or by an edge swipe. In the layout window, the Settings tile has its own field: a tile parked there is not shown in that layout. Each layout keeps its own choice.

Select the Settings tile to set:

  • PIN protection: ask for a 4–8 digit PIN before Settings opens.
  • Hide tile: park the tile in the layout the display shows.
  • Gear in the head: the same as Gear for Settings in the Head bar tab.

The public factory PIN 466384537 unlocks Settings and protected folders. This is a local child lock, not a login; protect the Web Admin itself with a Web Admin password. PINs are excluded from dashboard exports.

docs.title: Screensaver Editor
docs.text:
Open the Screensaver tab. Select the background, clock, or a tile to edit it; drag to move and resize.

See the Screensaver guide for images, activation, and available tiles. Its Tile borders setting is independent of the global Tile borders for the normal dashboard.

docs.title: Device Settings
docs.text:
Settings lists the same pages as the display:

  • WiFi: WiFi credentials, connection type on Ethernet-capable devices, and an optional static IP shared by WiFi and Ethernet.
  • Localization: language, time zone, date/time formats, and the first day of the week for the Energy popup, the Calendar, and the 30-day graph lines.
  • System: firmware update, the icon file, the connection to Home Assistant, pairing, and the Web Admin password. The MQTT settings are folded in here; while the direct link is active they stay saved but unused.
  • I/O: local hardware.
  • Built-in camera: on displays with a camera, see below.
  • Files and Diagnostics: see below.
Device settings in the Web Admin

docs.title: Icons
docs.text:
All 7447 Material Design Icons live in an icon file in the display's internal storage; 399 common icons, including Home Assistant's default icons, are built into the firmware. Without a valid icon file the display shows the built-in icons and a placeholder for the others.

A display without the file downloads it from the GitHub release of its own firmware version and restarts. If that fails, it tries again on the next restarts, up to three times per firmware version. Displays flashed with a factory image already have the file.

The Icons card below the firmware update shows the file:

  • Present: the file name, the number of icons and a check mark.
  • Missing or not usable: a download link to the right file for this display and firmware version (hometiles-icons-<size>.bin), the built-in and total icon count (for example 399 / 7447), and in red why the last download or install failed. Update makes the display download the file now, also after three failed attempts.

If the display cannot reach GitHub, for example behind a firewall, download the file with the link on your computer, select it under Icon file with Choose file, and press Update. The display checks the file before it installs it and refuses one that does not match its firmware's icons, such as a file for another icon size.

The screen stays dark while the display downloads the file or installs an uploaded one. It restarts afterwards, also after a failure, and the page reloads when it answers again.

docs.title: Web Admin Password
docs.text:
The Web Admin is open to everyone on your network by default. A password protects every page and API request, including the settings, restart, firmware upload, the file manager, and screenshots. On a paired display it also lets the entity picker find every Home Assistant entity, and locks and alarm panels need it.

  1. On the display, open Settings → System → Security and tap Allow next to Web Admin password.
  2. Within two minutes, enter the new password twice under Settings → System and select Set password.

Only someone at the display can set the first password.

  • The password is never sent in plain text: the browser proves it with a one-time challenge, and the display stores only a derived key.
  • Wrong passwords lock the sign-in for an increasing time, up to five minutes.
  • You stay signed in for 30 days, also after a restart or update of the display. Sign out ends the browser session; Remove password opens the Web Admin to the network again.
  • Forgot the password? On the display, open Settings → System → Security and remove it.
Web Admin password Sign-in page

docs.title: Built-in Camera
docs.text:
Displays with a supported camera show this section. Allow Home Assistant to use the built-in camera is off by default. When enabled, the display captures still images or a live stream only while the HomeTiles Bridge requests them.

Built-in camera settings
  • Mode: resolution, frame rate, and JPEG quality of the live stream. Higher values need more bandwidth.
  • Recording indicator: a red line at the top of the display and a circle in the head (a pill in the classic layout) to end the stream while the camera is in use.
  • Advanced: rotation, mirroring, and a red/blue swap for boards whose colors come out swapped.
  • Image: brightness, contrast, saturation, red and blue balance, and the maximum gain for dark rooms. Reset restores the defaults.

docs.title: Local Hardware I/O
docs.text: Open I/O to configure outputs, relays, or DS18B20 sensors. Only pins available for the selected device are offered. See Local Hardware I/O for setup and wiring.

docs.title: Import / Export
docs.text:
Export saves folders, tiles, the places of every layout, the pages and the screensaver in one JSON file. It excludes local I/O assignments and PINs. Older files without layouts or screensaver data leave those unchanged.

Import and export settings

Warning

Import replaces the folders, tiles, and screensaver data contained in the file.

docs.title: Screenshot & Diagnostics
docs.text:
Screenshot and diagnostics
  • Create & Download Screenshot: saves and downloads a JPEG of the current screen; requires microSD.
  • Download crash log: downloads reset reasons and crash details.
  • Open SD diagnostics: runs a short write and read test on the microSD card and shows the report.
  • Core dump: download or delete a stored memory snapshot when one is available.

See Reporting a crash for the files and details to include.

docs.title: Firmware Update
docs.text:
Check for releases or upload the matching OTA .bin under Settings → System. Follow Firmware Updates for the steps.

Firmware update

docs.title: File Manager
docs.text:
With a FAT32 microSD card inserted, use the file manager to upload, download, rename, or delete files and create folders. A card is optional for normal dashboard use.

microSD file manager

docs.title: Release Notes

These notes describe each release at publication. For current hardware support and fixes, see the device list.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.5.0
docs.text: This release introduces the new configurable screensaver and refreshes the visual and editing experience across HomeTiles.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Dedicated screensaver editor with live preview in the web admin
  • JPEG slideshow from /images on microSD, with image selection, ordering, shuffle, global duration, zoom, and focus controls
  • Freely movable and resizable clock with time/date/weekday options, alignment, larger fonts, and text shadow
  • Sensor, Energy, Switch, Scene, and Media tiles in the bottom two screensaver rows
  • Optional tile shadows, subtle borders, and per-tile opacity
  • Automatic screensaver timeout in Settings → Display; Clock tiles still open it immediately
  • Hardware-assisted image preparation across the Waveshare 4B, Waveshare 8-inch, and M5Stack Tab5 profiles
  • New Inter UI font and multiple web-admin usability improvements, including multi-file uploads, live entity refresh, persistent tabs, and improved previews
  • Screensaver-aware import/export with backward compatibility for older backups
  • Aggregated Energy Dashboard values now appear in the web preview
  • Stability improvements for PPA rendering, WiFi/SDIO traffic, MQTT commands, sensor history, energy statistics, and media covers

docs.title: microSD Setup
docs.text: Create /images in the root of a FAT32 microSD card and place .jpg or .jpeg files inside. Each file may be up to 8 MB; 1280×800 or 1920×1080 is recommended for fast loading. See the full Screensaver guide.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: The release contains firmware builds for all supported HomeTiles devices. Existing tile layouts and older JSON exports remain supported.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.5.1
docs.text: This maintenance release refines the new screensaver editor and adds a matching visual option for the normal dashboard.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Optional subtle tile borders across the complete normal dashboard
  • A global Settings → Display checkbox that updates every normal web preview and every normal on-device tile while keeping the screensaver setting separate
  • Fixed the unwanted green focus rectangle shown after clicking web-admin checkboxes
  • Renamed the screensaver background section from Screensaver / Wallpapers to Slideshow / Images for clearer terminology
  • Improved contrast and consistency in the slideshow image controls

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Existing installations default to enabled subtle borders and can turn them off at any time. Tile layouts, screensaver settings, and older JSON exports remain compatible. The release contains builds for every supported HomeTiles device.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.5.3
docs.text: This maintenance release improves CCT-only light handling and prevents interactive Energy and history requests from being blocked by MQTT control traffic.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• CCT-only lights are identified from Home Assistant's explicit supported_color_modes capabilities
  • The unsupported color palette stays hidden for lights that only provide color temperature, while brightness and Kelvin controls remain available
  • Converted rgb_color and hs_color state attributes no longer incorrectly turn a CCT-only light into a full-color light
  • CCT-only light tiles use the selected warm-to-cool Kelvin color and remain gray while switched off
  • Legacy light payloads without supported_color_modes retain the previous capability-detection fallback
  • MQTT publishes are separated from throttled subscribe/unsubscribe traffic so Energy, history, media, and light commands can continue to flow
  • Large MQTT buffers are requested together with the publish that needs them, avoiding queue-wide stalls and unnecessary buffer churn
  • Energy requests track pending responses and retry with bounded backoff instead of repeatedly filling the outbound queue

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: No configuration migration is required. Existing RGB, RGBW, RGBWW, XY, brightness, and simple on/off lights keep their previous controls. The release contains builds for every currently supported HomeTiles device.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.0
docs.text: HomeTiles v0.6.0 introduces a complete Climate tile and popup system, improves network transport reliability, and polishes the web editor and on-device UI across every supported display.

docs.title: Configurable Climate Tiles
docs.text:
• Climate tiles now contain a configurable grid of mini-tiles.
  • Mini-tiles can show current temperature, current humidity, target temperature, separate heating and cooling targets, target humidity, or HVAC mode.
  • Mini-tiles can be selected, moved, removed, and rearranged directly in the web preview.
  • Resizing a Climate tile updates its slot grid and layout live.
  • Automatic content uses the capabilities reported by the Home Assistant entity, so unsupported controls stay hidden.
  • Empty Climate tiles remain empty until an entity is selected.
  • Web previews and the LVGL device renderer use matching geometry, spacing, alignment, value formatting, and translated labels.
Climate tiles with different mini-tile layouts

docs.title: Climate Control Popup
docs.text:
The new touch-first popup adapts to each entity and can expose:

  • a single target temperature or a low/high target range
  • target humidity
  • HVAC modes
  • presets
  • fan modes
  • vertical swing modes
  • horizontal swing modes

Only supported controls are shown. Long custom option lists are smoothly touch-scrollable without a visible scrollbar. Current temperature and humidity, target markers, labels, and the circular control are aligned for both 720p and 800p layouts. Marker colors also update while a target is being dragged.

Rapid plus/minus input is handled without stale state updates causing the value to jump backwards.

Climate popup with all supported controls Heat-only Climate popup

docs.title: Web Editor And Localization
docs.text:
• Parent tiles and mini-tiles have distinct selection, hover, and drag feedback.
  • Dragging a mini-tile no longer selects or moves its parent.
  • Parent resize previews keep mini-tile geometry stable in every direction.
  • Climate labels use the shared localization profile instead of language-specific JavaScript branches.
  • German and English captions remain consistent between settings, web previews, and the device UI.

docs.title: Network And Stability
docs.text:
• Added a shared network transport layer with improved WiFi/Ethernet takeover and fallback behavior.
  • Improved UI responsiveness while network transports reconnect.
  • Hardened ESP-Hosted SDIO transmit and receive allocation paths used by the ESP32-P4/ESP32-C6 connection.
  • Existing crash diagnostics and safe recovery remain available through the web admin.

docs.title: Supported Devices
docs.text:
Every release includes OTA and factory binaries for:

  • M5Stack Tab5
  • Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-4B
  • Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-8

Use the plain .bin for an OTA update and the _factory.bin only for the first USB flash. See Firmware Updates for the complete instructions.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.1
docs.text: HomeTiles v0.6.1 is a focused network safety, Web Admin reliability, and UI polish release. It unifies WiFi and Ethernet addressing, adds a safe DHCP recovery path on the device, and removes disruptive full-page reloads when settings are saved.

docs.title: Shared Network Configuration
docs.text:
• WiFi and Ethernet now use one shared DHCP/static-IP selection and one shared set of IP address, gateway, subnet mask, and DNS values.
  • Static addressing is applied consistently to WiFi, native Ethernet, and USB Ethernet.
  • Existing installations with separate experimental Ethernet values are migrated to the shared profile.
  • Selecting WiFi or Ethernet changes only the transport used after restart; it no longer swaps or hides a different IP profile.
  • Incomplete or invalid static settings safely fall back to DHCP.

docs.title: DHCP Recovery On The Device
docs.text:
• The network popup shows Use DHCP only when the device actually booted with a static address.
  • Selecting a static address in the Web Admin for the next boot does not prematurely show the recovery action.
  • After Use DHCP is pressed, Undo DHCP remains available until restart.
  • A restart or normal power cycle applies the saved selection. After a DHCP boot, the recovery action disappears again.
  • The same behavior is available on WiFi-only devices and Ethernet-capable devices.

docs.title: Web Admin And Display Updates
docs.text:
• Network and MQTT settings are saved in the background, so the Web Admin no longer turns black while the complete page is regenerated and reloaded.
  • The Save button briefly confirms a successful background save.
  • If the on-device network popup is open while settings are saved in the Web Admin, its content is rebuilt in one pass. Updated buttons and status messages appear without stale blocks or misplaced controls.
  • Network settings use clearer WiFi, Ethernet, and IP-configuration grouping.
  • Save and Restart actions stay accessible at the bottom of the settings view.
  • Browser-provided IP address suggestions keep the HomeTiles field styling.

docs.title: UI Polish
docs.text:
• Increased spacing between the navigation controls in the light popup.
  • Updated German and English network labels, including the DHCP recovery and undo actions.

docs.title: Supported Devices
docs.text:
Every release includes OTA and factory binaries for:

  • M5Stack Tab5
  • Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-4B
  • Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-8
  • ESP32-P4-86-Panel-ETH-2RO with Ethernet (uses the Waveshare 4B firmware)

Thanks to @onikserj for testing Ethernet support on the ESP32-P4-86-Panel-ETH-2RO and for the feedback that led to the shared static-IP configuration and improved light-popup spacing.

Use the plain .bin for an OTA update and the _factory.bin only for the first USB flash. See Firmware Updates for the complete instructions.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.10
docs.text: HomeTiles v0.6.10 adds editable value tiles and Home Assistant view control, supports another Waveshare display, and brings the confirmed Guition JC8012 V1 Camera/Web OTA fix into a regular release.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• S3 GitHub OTA: the downloader can fall back to PSRAM when internal memory is insufficient on Guition ESP32-4848S040, Waveshare S3 LCD-4, and S3 LCD-4B. P4 images are unchanged.
  • Number, Select, and Date/Time tiles: control number / input_number, select / input_select, and time / date / datetime / input_datetime entities. Number includes a graph and Activity; Select combines a state timeline with Activity; Date/Time shows Activity. All use 24-hour and 7-day history where HA Recorder data is available.
  • Controls that fit the display: centered Media-style sliders, Climate-style temperature steppers, Settings dropdowns, and single-row time rollers with wraparound. Edits tolerate delayed device responses. The control, history, and Activity layout adapts to the available screen area, and control colors follow the popup background.
  • Home Assistant View control: an additional Select on the existing display device opens Home, nested folders, or a configured popup. Manual navigation reports the actual view back to HA. Existing PIN checks and camera cleanup remain in effect; stale commands are rejected after reconnect or restart.
  • More compatible entities: Switch tiles also handle Toggle helpers, automations, fans, humidifiers, remotes, and sirens where on/off is supported. Scene tiles can press button and input_button entities. Automation on/off enables or disables triggers rather than running the actions immediately.
  • Two-line titles and value sizes: press Enter for a second centered title line; overflow uses ... according to the tile and display size. Popup headers and Web Admin previews follow the same title. Number, Select, and Date/Time now share Sensor's five value-size choices and display their current values in the Web preview.
  • Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4, Rev 4.0: a dedicated release and browser-installer profile for the 480×480 board with CH32V003-assisted display/backlight initialization. This is separate from the P4 Waveshare 4B and the S3 LCD-4B. Older LCD-4 revisions and SD access are unsupported.
  • Guition JC8012P4A1 V1: the field-confirmed SDIO receive fix is now included in the regular image. It addresses the transport failure that caused camera crashes and Web Admin OTA failures. The fix remains limited to this exact V1 profile; other P4 boards keep their established transport variant.
  • MQTT, icons, and popup fixes: larger valid configuration packets no longer hit the former 16 KiB receive limit; icon refresh handles delayed metadata; dropdown redraw work and history range switching are improved. Multiline titles no longer invalidate a display's View options.
  • Sensor cleanup: the companion Bridge removes obsolete automatically generated battery/temperature entries using ownership and reported capabilities, while retaining supported local I/O and explicit user selections.
  • Maintenance and documentation: smaller generated Web Admin delivery, shared browser/server helpers, clearer subsystem ownership, and expanded native UI, browser, persistence, and protocol regression coverage. The documentation and installer now describe the complete feature set and exact device variants.

docs.title: Update Notes
docs.text:
If S3 device OTA fails, install the corrected regular BIN through Web Admin once. Devices already reporting v0.6.10 also need a manual update to receive this same-version correction.

Use HomeTiles Bridge v0.6.44 or newer for the complete feature set and icon fixes. Update it through HACS and restart Home Assistant. That Bridge is already released and remains compatible with older firmware and configurations; this firmware release does not require a new Bridge release.

Existing layouts remain compatible, and existing tile type IDs are preserved. Add the new editable entities in Bridge Entity Configuration, then assign them in Web Admin. View option labels include their path and target suffix; update automation option text after renaming or moving a target.

Use the regular .bin for OTA or the browser installer's Update mode. Use _factory.bin only for first installation or an intentional factory reset. The release contains 15 exact installer profiles, each with an OTA and factory image.

Choose the exact board and revision. The new S3 LCD-4 image is for Rev 4.0 only. Waveshare 7B/7B-C has separate pre-v3 and exact ESP32-P4 v3.1 images; v3.2 and newer remain unsupported by the pinned toolchain. Camera remains experimental and ESP32-P4-only.

docs.title: Hardware Confirmed
docs.text:
• The corrected Guition ESP32-4848S040 downloader completed all 11 GitHub download ranges on the first attempt, installed v0.6.10, and reconnected to MQTT after restart.
  • The maintainer reports the current editable controls and dashboard changes working on Waveshare Touch LCD 8-inch and Guition ESP32-4848S040 ESP32-S3 after the local test builds.
  • The Guition JC8012 V1 reporter confirmed stable camera streams and successful Web Admin OTA in the integrated v0.6.9b1 test build, following the successful b6 transport test. This release carries that same exact-profile fix.
  • The Waveshare LCD-4 Rev 4.0 contributor confirmed display, backlight, touch, Wi-Fi, Web Admin, MQTT/Bridge integration, and Web OTA on physical hardware in PR #35.

docs.title: Pending Hardware Validation
docs.text:
GitHub OTA with this correction on Waveshare S3 LCD-4 and S3 LCD-4B still awaits field confirmation.

CI builds every release profile; this is compile and packaging coverage, not proof of runtime behavior on every board. The new UI paths on other devices and exact revisions still need field testing. Existing device-specific SD, OTA, Ethernet, and camera validation limits remain listed in the device support notes.

An earlier isolated Guition S3 display freeze while adding a Number tile to an active screensaver has not been conclusively explained. The display recovered after a manual restart; continued reproduction and diagnostics are still needed. The MQTT correction for issue #37 also awaits confirmation from that reporter.

Thanks to @verrat73 for the Waveshare LCD-4 Rev 4.0 contribution and to @pguns for testing the Guition JC8012 V1 transport fix.

S3 correction source: 766efc1. The six S3 images were rebuilt from this commit; the Git tag and P4 images remain unchanged.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/GalusPeres/HomeTiles/compare/v0.6.9...v0.6.10

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.11
docs.text: v0.6.11 improves popup responsiveness and media artwork stability, fixes Weather and PIN titles, and adds browser device logs with USB sessions that stay connected while browsing the documentation.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Improved popup opening by reusing the shared frame, header and close button with cached content. Corrected tile press styles remove unnecessary layout work, including the noticeable delay when opening large Weather tiles.
  • Stabilized media artwork during track changes and state updates. The current cover remains visible while its replacement loads or fails, and text keeps its position. Cover handling also avoids unnecessary downloads and stale image results.
  • Aligned Weather values with Sensor tiles and kept the same top position on larger tiles, with forecasts below. Device rendering and Web Admin previews now share consistent headers, two-line titles and text truncation.
  • Fixed reused PIN popups showing the preloaded Settings title. Protected tiles now display their own unlock prompt, such as Radio. The correction uses the shared implementation on P4 and S3 devices.
  • Added browser device logs with live USB serial capture, copy and clear controls, and a saved log snapshot. The logger works directly in supported desktop Chrome and Edge browsers without installing a separate serial monitor.
  • Kept logger and flasher sessions active across documentation pages, search and browser back/forward. The header displays USB activity and flash progress. Port ownership is coordinated, and cancelling the flasher's port chooser leaves logging running.
  • Expanded regression coverage for native LVGL interaction, Weather rendering, title reuse, Web Admin previews and browser USB navigation. All 98 tests passed before the release build.

docs.title: Update Notes
docs.text:
Use HomeTiles Bridge v0.6.44 or newer for the complete feature set. No new Bridge release is required. Existing layouts and configurations remain compatible.

Use the regular .bin for OTA or the browser installer's Update mode. Use _factory.bin only for first installation or an intentional factory reset. All 15 release profiles include both images; select the exact board and revision.

Internal documentation navigation preserves USB connections. A full page reload restores captured log text but requires reconnecting to resume live capture.

docs.title: Hardware Confirmed
docs.text:
The shared UI improvements were tested on Waveshare Touch LCD 8-inch, Waveshare 4B, Guition ESP32-4848S040 S3 and M5Stack Tab5. Large Weather tile responsiveness and title truncation were confirmed on 8-inch; the final PIN title correction on Tab5.

The maintainer also tested browser flashing locally. Automated browser tests cover retained sessions and USB handoff using simulated hardware transport.

docs.title: Pending Hardware Validation
docs.text:
All 15 profiles built successfully. Other devices, exact revisions and extended media, navigation and sleep/wake testing still need field feedback. Compilation does not establish physical behavior on every board.

Camera remains experimental and P4-only. Existing validation limits, including Waveshare S3 GitHub OTA and exact P4 v3.1 hardware, remain in the device support notes. The isolated S3 screensaver freeze and external MQTT issue #37 still await confirmation.

Thanks to everyone testing HomeTiles and reporting reproducible issues.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/GalusPeres/HomeTiles/compare/v0.6.10...v0.6.11

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.12
docs.text: v0.6.12 accelerates the Guition JC8012P4A1 V1/V2 interface and corrects Weather forecast positioning and daily temperature labels.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Enabled PPA hardware rotation for larger ordinary UI updates on Guition JC8012P4A1 V1 and V2. These updates previously rotated on the CPU even when PPA was initialized. Small regions retain the CPU fallback, with shared timeout and recovery handling.
  • Aligned the Weather forecast row on both Guition revisions with the existing Waveshare 8-inch and 10.1-inch position. All four profiles share the same 1280x800 grid; the Guition forecast was 10 pixels too low.
  • Preserved the weather provider's daily minimum and maximum when hourly data covers only part of the day. Partial hourly forecasts no longer replace the full-day temperature labels.
  • Improved browser USB log instructions and cleared stale flashing results when starting a new session.

docs.title: Update Notes
docs.text:
Use HomeTiles Bridge v0.6.44 or newer for the complete feature set. No new Bridge release is required. Existing layouts and configurations remain compatible.

Use the regular .bin for OTA or the browser installer's Update mode. Use _factory.bin only for first installation or an intentional factory reset. Select the exact board and revision: Guition JC8012P4A1 V1 and V2 require different images.

The V1-specific ESP-Hosted network mitigation is preserved. This release does not change the Guition SD implementation or the Waveshare 8-inch display driver.

docs.title: Hardware Confirmed
docs.text: The maintainer confirmed that the PPA correction resolves the reported slow interface on Guition JC8012P4A1 V2. The maintainer also reports working SD-card access with the existing SD implementation.

docs.title: Pending Hardware Validation
docs.text:
The corresponding V1 acceleration and forecast-position correction still need testing on an actual V1 device. Host regression tests cover both rotation directions, PPA/CPU fallback, timeout ownership and recovery, and matching forecast coordinates across all 35 supported tile spans. These tests and successful firmware compilation do not establish physical V1 behavior.

The daily temperature-label correction has focused regression coverage; broader provider and device feedback remains welcome. The SD-card reboot reported in issue #38 is not reproduced on the maintainer's V2 and is not claimed fixed here. Existing camera, networking and exact-revision limitations remain in the device support notes.

Thanks to everyone testing HomeTiles, including the contributors who provided the original V2 panel data and reported the Weather problems.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/GalusPeres/HomeTiles/compare/v0.6.11...v0.6.12

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.2
docs.text: HomeTiles v0.6.2 adds official release support for the 10.1-inch Guition JC8012P4A1C_I_W_Y and fixes Bridge setup for newly added devices.

docs.title: Guition JC8012P4A1C_I_W_Y
docs.text:
• Added factory and OTA binaries for guition_jc8012p4a1.
  • Integrated the 1280×800 display, brightness control and GSL3680 touch.
  • Added microSD support and dual-partition OTA for the board's 16MB flash.
  • Confirmed MQTT communication, Home Assistant Bridge data and automatic discovery on real hardware.
  • Corrected the touch direction so input matches the displayed interface.

The implementation uses the Apache-2.0-compatible touch path documented in the device source directory.

Many thanks to @brmo for sharing the original working display code, testing the HomeTiles builds on the device, and providing the detailed logs and feedback needed to finish the integration.

docs.title: MQTT And Bridge
docs.text:
• Fixed Bridge setup for newly added devices. HomeTiles now sends its MAC-based Bridge announcement after every MQTT connection, allowing the Home Assistant integration to return the selected entity list.
  • Prevented a Bridge apply/announce feedback loop.
  • The bug was easy to miss because existing devices already had retained Bridge data and continued to work normally.

docs.title: Other Changes
docs.text:
• Expanded the translation groundwork and moved more UI text into the shared i18n tables.
  • The unfinished French language option remains hidden for now.

Use the regular .bin file for OTA updates and the _factory.bin file only for the initial USB flash.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.3
docs.text: HomeTiles v0.6.3 adds an experimental camera popup for ESP32-P4 displays, improves light controls and network stability, adds Cyrillic tile-title glyphs, and removes unfinished non-Home-Assistant features.

docs.title: Upgrade Order
docs.text:
1. Update HomeTiles Bridge to v0.6.28 through HACS and restart Home Assistant.
  2. Update the display to HomeTiles v0.6.3.
  3. For Camera tiles, select the camera under HomeTiles Bridge → Configure → Entity Configuration.

Other tile types continue to work without the camera protocol, but Camera tiles explicitly require Bridge v0.6.28 or newer.

docs.title: Experimental Camera Popup
docs.text:
• Added Camera tiles and a popup that fills the available 16:9 content area.
  • Supports Home Assistant cameras with a direct stream source as well as snapshot-only camera entities.
  • The Bridge uses FFmpeg to produce display-sized JPEG frames and sends them through an acknowledged local TCP connection. MQTT remains active for normal states, commands and camera setup.
  • The display requests its own popup geometry, so each P4 profile uses the same camera implementation without hard-coded device names.
  • Direct streams can reach up to 24 FPS. Actual performance is limited by the source frame rate, Home Assistant host, network and display.
  • Added bounded buffering, latest-frame replacement, triple display buffers and protected presentation paths so camera work cannot consume the MQTT/WiFi reserve.
  • Added explicit camera protocol negotiation and a translated Bridge-update message instead of waiting indefinitely on an incompatible integration.
  • Camera sessions use the first available local TCP port from 8124 to 8131.

Camera support is experimental. FFmpeg transcoding consumes CPU on the Home Assistant host, and every simultaneously open panel creates a separate session. The ESP32-S3 Guition ESP32-4848S040C_I does not expose Camera tiles.

docs.title: Lights And CCT
docs.text:
• Reworked brightness, color-wheel and color-temperature interaction so local feedback follows the finger without flooding Home Assistant with every touch sample.
  • Preserved the existing popup design while fixing redraw gaps and rounded slider endpoints.
  • CCT-only lights keep brightness, power and Kelvin controls while hiding the unsupported color palette.
  • Warm/cold endpoint requests use the exact Kelvin range reported by Home Assistant. Current Waveshare 4B, Waveshare 8 and the previous Tab5 firmware were checked with a two-channel CCT test entity.

docs.title: Text And Interface
docs.text:
• Added modern Cyrillic glyphs to tile-title fonts in the common 14, 16, 20 and 24 px sizes (issue #10).
  • English and German remain the selectable complete interface languages.
  • French stays hidden while its translation pass is unfinished.

docs.title: Stability And Maintenance
docs.text:
• Moved additional ESP-Hosted receive allocations to PSRAM and retained the patched TX path used by release builds.
  • Restored the normal UI draw buffer after closing a camera popup instead of leaving later popups on the large video buffer.
  • Kept MQTT and WiFi active during camera streaming and bounded frame transport with receiver acknowledgements.
  • Removed the unfinished PC WebSocket server, desktop companion application, Flight Simulator bridge, Key tiles and Counter tiles.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.4
docs.text: v0.6.4 improves long-term stability and responsiveness and adds configurable local hardware I/O.

docs.title: Upgrade Order
docs.text:
1. Update HomeTiles Bridge to v0.6.32 through HACS and restart Home Assistant.
  2. Update the display to HomeTiles v0.6.4.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Faster folder navigation, Weather popups and tile restoration, including during long sessions.
  • Light brightness, color and Kelvin sliders reliably send the newest value and both endpoints while remaining rate-limited.
  • Separate screensaver brightness and more reliable idle handling, including open Camera popups.
  • New I/O tab for up to eight local switches, onboard relays or DS18B20 sensors. Local tiles work directly on the panel; Bridge v0.6.32 adds the entities to Home Assistant.
  • Faster web-admin loading and refresh behavior.
  • Improved ESP-Hosted RPC/SDIO recovery and diagnostics. The safe-restart fallback remains for unresolved upstream WiFi/C6 lockups.

Camera support on ESP32-P4 remains experimental. The Guition ESP32-4848S040 ESP32-S3 image also remains experimental and does not support Camera tiles.

Hardware-confirmed targets are M5Stack Tab5, Waveshare 4B/86 Panel/8-inch and Guition JC8012. Waveshare 7/10.1-inch, Guition JC1060 and Guition ESP32-S3 remain community-test images.

Use the regular .bin for OTA and _factory.bin only for the first USB flash or a complete reset.

docs.title: HomeTiles v0.6.5
docs.text: v0.6.5 adds Home Assistant Cover controls and improves display, storage and interaction stability across all published device profiles.

docs.title: Upgrade Order
docs.text:
1. Update HomeTiles Bridge to v0.6.35 through HACS and restart Home Assistant.
  2. Update the display to HomeTiles v0.6.5.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• New localized Cover tiles and a Light-popup-based Cover popup with feature-aware position, tilt, open, close and stop controls.
  • Improved Guition ESP32-S3 touch, RGB display synchronization, OTA, screenshots, slideshow memory use and rate-limited diagnostics.
  • Unified normal and screensaver brightness across device UI, MQTT and Home Assistant without losing the safe device-specific PWM ranges.
  • Expanded the folder cache to six grids across all ESP32-P4 profiles and moved cold renderer bookkeeping into PSRAM to reclaim internal RAM.
  • Added a live downloadable SD diagnostic report without persistent diagnostic history.
  • Added a separate image for Guition JC8012P4A1 V2 (SKU:10153002-V2).
  • Corrected JC1060 SD startup by applying the board's active-low GPIO45 power reset before mounting the card.

The Guition ESP32-4848S040 ESP32-S3 image is hardware-tested and does not support Camera tiles.

Hardware-confirmed targets are M5Stack Tab5, Waveshare 4B/86 Panel/8-inch, Guition JC8012 V1 and Guition ESP32-S3. Waveshare 7/10.1-inch and Guition JC8012 V2 still need complete physical-device validation. JC1060 SD-card operation still needs confirmation on the exact _I_W_Y hardware.

Use the regular .bin for OTA and _factory.bin only for the first USB flash or a complete reset.
